_meta.description: Per-material SKIN-CONTACT safety floor for FDM parts worn or handled against intact skin (rings, bands, grips, earbud shells, jewelry, glasses, masks). Advisory RISK-STRATIFICATION, never certification: no 3D-printed part is skin-safe, hypoallergenic, or biocompatible. This public file is the always-free safety floor (honesty note + named hazards + the refer-to-medical boundary) so the caution reaches every install, offline included. Per-exposure verdicts, the remediation playbook, and the regulated-market compliance mapping are Kiln Pro/Business/Enterprise.
_meta._split_note: Safety floor only. The per-exposure verdict, remediation depth (which standard applies, what test answers it, sealing / cleanability), and the REACH / toy-safety compliance layer are curated in Kiln Pro. See https://kiln3d.com/pricing.
_meta.prime_directive: There is NO affirmative skin-safe verdict. 'No data' is returned as caution, never as safety. Out-of-scope uses (mouth/eye/mucosal, broken skin, piercing, implant, children's mouthing) are out of scope for a printed part — refer to a medical professional and a certified medical-grade material.

exposure_tiers.incidental: surface / intact skin, limited (<=24h) — brief handling
exposure_tiers.prolonged: surface / intact skin, prolonged (>24h) — worn items
exposure_tiers.mucosal: mucosal membrane — out of intact-skin scope
exposure_tiers.broken_implant: breached surface / implant / permanent — out of scope

pla.concern_basis: benign base polymer; risk is the undisclosed colorant/additive load

safety_floor.honesty_note: No 3D-printed PLA part is tested or certified skin-safe. PLA's benign reputation belongs to characterized medical-grade resin, not to a colored consumer spool.
named_hazards: undisclosed colorant/additive load (the dominant, unlabelled variable)
low softening temperature (Tg ~55-65 C) under warm, prolonged wear
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

pla_plus.concern_basis: as PLA plus undisclosed impact modifiers

safety_floor.honesty_note: 'PLA+' is a marketing term for PLA with proprietary, undisclosed impact modifiers; it is LESS characterized for skin than neat PLA, not safer.
named_hazards: undisclosed impact-modifier layer ON TOP OF the base colorant/additive load
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

silk_pla.concern_basis: as PLA plus undisclosed effect additives

safety_floor.honesty_note: Effect PLA adds undisclosed gloss or matting additives on top of the color; it is the least-characterized PLA for skin contact.
named_hazards: effect additives (silk gloss agents / matte mineral fillers) ON TOP OF the colorant load
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

petg.concern_basis: benign base with food-contact heritage; colorant load undisclosed

safety_floor.honesty_note: PETG's food-contact heritage is a good sign but is NOT a skin-safety certification; 'safe for a food container' is a different test from 'safe to wear on skin'.
named_hazards: undisclosed colorant/additive package (often the real sensitizer)
antimony trioxide polycondensation catalyst residue
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

abs.concern_basis: styrene (IARC Group 2A) + acrylonitrile (IARC Group 1 human carcinogen)

safety_floor.honesty_note: ABS contains two monomers of toxicological concern (styrene, acrylonitrile) and is not tested for skin contact; it is not recommended for worn items.
named_hazards: residual styrene (IARC Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans)
residual acrylonitrile (IARC Group 1 — carcinogenic to humans, Vol. 136 2025)
undisclosed flame-retardant / colorant package
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

asa.concern_basis: styrene (IARC Group 2A) + acrylonitrile (IARC Group 1 human carcinogen)

safety_floor.honesty_note: ASA replaces ABS's butadiene rubber with an acrylic-ester rubber for UV stability but retains the same two monomers of concern; its weather resistance does not improve its skin profile.
named_hazards: residual styrene (IARC Group 2A) + acrylonitrile (IARC Group 1, carcinogenic to humans) — as ABS
undisclosed weather-package / colorant additives
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

polycarbonate.concern_basis: BPA — endocrine disruptor, skin-absorbed, releases under heat/sweat

safety_floor.honesty_note: Polycarbonate is made from BPA, which leaches out with heat and sweat and is absorbed through skin; consumer PC spools are regular BPA-based (not BPA-free / medical) grades and are untested for skin.
named_hazards: bisphenol-A (BPA) — the structural monomer; releases under heat/sweat/abrasion
BPA is skin-absorbed and an endocrine disruptor
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

nylon.concern_basis: residual caprolactam is a skin/eye/respiratory irritant; hygroscopic

safety_floor.honesty_note: Nylon-6 is built from caprolactam, a classified skin/eye/respiratory irritant, and is strongly hygroscopic, so a worn part soaks up sweat and can leach residuals; no printed nylon is tested for skin.
named_hazards: residual caprolactam (skin/eye/respiratory irritant, CLP H315/H319/H335)
high moisture absorption — a worn part soaks and holds sweat
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

safety_floor.honesty_note: PA12 is a chemically milder nylon than PA6 (laurolactam-based, lower moisture uptake) but no printed PA12 part is tested for skin contact.
named_hazards: undisclosed colorant/additive load
hygroscopic (less than PA6, still absorbs sweat)
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

tpu.concern_basis: top wearable material; undisclosed plasticizer system, untested for skin

safety_floor.honesty_note: TPU is the top wearable material (bands, grips, earbud tips), which is exactly why the caution line is held hardest here: consumer TPU has no finished-part skin data and an undisclosed plasticizer system. 'Watch bands are made of TPU' is true — of CERTIFIED skin-contact TPU compounds, not an uncertified consumer spool.
named_hazards: undisclosed plasticizers / processing oils (the real skin-contact variable)
residual free isocyanate only if under-reacted (fully-reacted TPU has none)
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

cf_nylon.concern_basis: mechanical: exposed fiber ends cause skin irritation / micro-splinters

safety_floor.honesty_note: Fiber-filled filaments add a MECHANICAL hazard unfilled polymers do not: chopped carbon or glass fiber ends protrude at every cut, abraded, worn, or porous surface and act like fiberglass against skin, independent of chemistry.
named_hazards: exposed fiber ends at cut/abraded/worn/porous surfaces -> mechanical dermatitis / micro-splinters
respirable fiber dust during sanding (a lung hazard — fitted respirator, not a paper mask)
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

wood_fill.concern_basis: particulate/microbe harboring; wood dust is an inhalation carcinogen

safety_floor.honesty_note: Wood-look filament is a PLA-type matrix loaded with real wood particles; worn on skin it soaks up sweat and can harbor microbes, and sanding it makes wood dust (IARC Group 1).
named_hazards: wood particles harbor moisture/microbes and can cause mechanical/allergic irritation
wood dust (sanding) is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen by inhalation
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

metal_fill.concern_basis: nickel (leading contact allergen) + heavy-metal particulate release

safety_floor.honesty_note: Metal-look filament contains real metal powder that can release nickel and other metals into sweaty skin; nickel is the leading contact allergen and there is a legal release limit for worn items.
named_hazards: metal particulate can release nickel and other metals into sweaty skin over time
nickel is the most common contact allergen; a legal release limit exists
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

pp.concern_basis: lowest base-chemistry concern; colorant/additive load undisclosed

safety_floor.honesty_note: Raw PP has among the lowest base-chemistry concern of consumer plastics and a real olefin food-contact heritage, but food-contact clearance is NOT skin certification and the printed part's additives/porosity remain untested for skin.
named_hazards: undisclosed colorant/additive load
porous layer-line surface (hygiene)
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

safety_floor.honesty_note: PVA is a water-soluble support material; sweat will turn a worn PVA part gummy, so it is simply the wrong material to wear. That is a fitness-for-use fact, not a toxicology verdict.
named_hazards: dissolves in water/sweat — a worn part degrades
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: For implanted, broken-skin, mucosal (mouth/eye/in-canal), piercing-post, or children's-mouthing use, stop: this is out of scope for a printed part. See a medical professional and use a certified medical-grade material.

peek.concern_basis: certified grades are industrial-only; refer out

safety_floor.honesty_note: Implant-grade PEEK and medical PEI (ULTEM) are genuinely biocompatible, but that certification belongs to a qualified industrial material + process, not to anything a consumer desktop printer produces; do not treat it as a consumer skin-contact fix.
named_hazards: real biocompatible grades exist but require industrial printers (>350 C, heated chamber)
safety_floor.refer_to_medical: PEEK/PEI implant- and medical-grade materials are real but industrial-only. For any certified skin-contact or medical need, see a medical professional and a certified medical-grade supplier; a desktop-printed part is not a substitute.
